pass_b_english: Christ's sacrifice has the power to sanctify the people through his own blood, because he suffered not for his own sake, but for the sake of all people under heaven.
The worship prescribed by the law was unable to remove sins on earth, since sacrifices and sheep slaughters were displeasing to God.
However, the true lamb, who takes away the sin of the world, offered himself as a fragrant odor for us.
As Paul testifies in writing, God did not spare his own Son, but handed him over for us all, so that with him he may grant us all things.

Christ himself says through the Psalmist, 'You did not want a sacrifice and offering, but a body you prepared for me; you did not approve whole burnt offerings and sin offerings; then I said, "Behold, I come"; it is written in the scroll of the book about me, to do your will, O God' (Psalm 40:6-8).
Having endured the death of the flesh, Christ freed the whole world under heaven from death and sin, because one who is worthy of all suffered for all, so that he may rule and reign over all.
Paul also writes that Christ died and lived, so that he may be Lord of both the dead and the living.
One person died on behalf of all, so that those who are living would no longer live for themselves, but for the one who died and rose for them.
The prophet describes this person as one who knows how to bear weaknesses, has his face set towards the afflicted, is despised, and not considered, and who bears our sins and suffers for us.

We thought he was in pain, affliction, and evil, because we believed the passion happened to him as a divine punishment for some sins, and that because of that sin, he was in pain, affliction, and evil.
But it is not so; rather, he was wounded because of our sins and weakened because of our lawlessness.
The prophetic word proceeds with simplicity, and the face of those not knowing the mystery of Christ is hypocritical, thinking that he became afflicted due to his own sins.
We thought he was in pain, affliction, and evil, that is, we thought the passion happened to him as a divine punishment for some sins, and because of that sin, he was in pain, affliction, and evil.
But it is not so; rather, he was wounded because of our sins and weakened because of our lawlessness.
Then he gives other reasons, through which it can be seen that the sinless one suffered for the sake of our salvation and life.
For we were formerly at enmity with God, fighting against his holy laws, not having the yoke of obedience, and refusing to serve him.
